steps.title: Cut butter
points: Take the butter out of the fridge and cut it in two.
About 10 g goes in the pan, about 5 g on top at the end.
Leave the finishing piece out so it softens while you cook.

steps.title: Melt butter
points: Set the pan over low heat and add the 10 g piece.
Swirl it as it melts.
Stop as soon as the foam settles, before it browns.

steps.title: Toast first side
points: Lay the bread in and slide it around once so the underside drinks the butter.
Toast for 2 to 3 minutes, pressing gently with the spatula.
It is ready when the underside is deep golden brown.

steps.title: Toast second side
points: Flip the bread over.
Toast for 2 minutes more.
If the pan looks dry, run a sliver of butter along the edge and tilt it underneath.

steps.title: Top with butter
points: Move the toast to a plate and set the softened butter in the middle.
Add the pinch of salt or a thread of honey if you like.
Eat it right away, while the outside still crackles.

steps.title: Beat eggs
points: Beat the eggs in a bowl with the pinch of salt.
Mix until the yolks and whites are fully combined, no streaks.

steps.title: Slice spring onion
points: Slice the spring onion thinly.
Keep the white and the green parts in separate piles.

steps.title: Heat rice
points: Microwave the packed rice as directed.
Have it hot and beside the stove before the pan goes on.

steps.title: Scramble eggs
points: Heat the oil over medium-high until it shimmers, then pour in the eggs.
Let them sit for 10 seconds, then stir with chopsticks for about 30 seconds.
Scoop them back into the bowl while the curds are still a little wet.

steps.title: Fry rice
points: Add the white parts of the spring onion and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the hot rice, press it flat with the spatula, and let it sit for 30 seconds before folding.
Repeat the press and fold for about 2 minutes, until the grains jump loose in the pan.

steps.title: Add soy sauce
points: Pour the soy sauce around the rim of the pan, not onto the rice, and toss immediately.
It hits the bare metal, sizzles, and goes in toasty rather than wet.
Add the white pepper, then the sesame oil or butter if using.

steps.title: Return eggs
points: Tip the eggs back in along with the green parts of the spring onion.
Break the curds up with the spatula.
Fold everything together for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Plate fried rice
points: Taste, and adjust with a little salt.
Mound it onto a plate while it is still steaming.

steps.title: Mix the custard
points: Crack the egg into the shallow bowl and add the sugar.
Beat with chopsticks until the yolk, white and sugar are one even yellow.
Stir in the milk and the pinch of salt if you are using them.

steps.title: Soak the bread
points: Lay a slice flat in the custard and leave it for a minute.
Turn it over and give the second side the same minute.
Press the middle gently with your fingertip: it should feel heavy and damp, not soggy.

steps.title: Melt the butter
points: Set the pan over low heat and add about 10 g of butter.
Swirl it so it coats the whole base.
Stop as soon as the foam settles, before it takes on any color.

steps.title: Fry the first side
points: Lift the bread out, let the drips fall back into the bowl, and lay it in the pan.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes without moving it.
Lift a corner: the underside should be an even golden brown.

steps.title: Fry the second side
points: Flip with the spatula and add the last of the butter along the edge of the pan.
Cook for 3 minutes more, with the lid on if the slices are thick.
Press the centre with the spatula. It should spring back rather than squash.

steps.title: Serve
points: Move both slices to a plate and cut them across on the diagonal.
Pour over maple syrup while the surface is still hot enough to thin it out.
Eat straight away, before the crust softens.

steps.title: Prep garlic
points: Peel all four cloves. Slice one of them as thin as you can manage, and dice the other three fine.
Keep the two piles separate. The slices turn into crisp chips, the diced garlic flavors the rice.
Even thickness matters more than thinness, because uneven slices burn at different times.

steps.title: Heat rice
points: Microwave the packed rice as directed.
Break it up with the spatula while it is still hot, and leave it beside the stove.
Rice that goes in as a solid block never separates properly.

steps.title: Crisp garlic slices
points: Put the sliced garlic and the oil into the pan together, then turn the heat to low.
Starting from cold dries the garlic out slowly instead of scorching it.
Stir now and then for about 4 minutes, until the slices are pale gold at the edges.

steps.title: Lift out chips
points: Scoop the slices onto the paper-lined plate the moment they turn pale gold.
Spread them in a single layer so they crisp as they cool.
Leave the oil in the pan. That is where most of the garlic flavor now lives.

steps.title: Cook diced garlic
points: Turn the heat up to medium. If you are using sausage, cut it into thick coins and brown them in the garlic oil for about 2 minutes, then push them to one side of the pan.
Add the diced garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells sweet and the edges just start to color.
Drop in the butter and swirl the pan until it melts.

steps.title: Fry rice
points: Turn the heat to medium-high and tip in the hot rice.
Press it flat with the spatula and leave it alone for 30 seconds before folding it over.
Repeat the press and fold for about 2 minutes, until the grains separate and jump loose in the pan.

steps.title: Season rice
points: Pour the soy sauce around the rim of the pan so it hits bare metal and sizzles, then toss straight away.
Add the pinch of salt and a good grind of black pepper.
Taste it, and reach for more salt rather than more soy sauce if it needs lifting.

steps.title: Plate and top
points: Turn off the heat, drizzle over the sesame oil if using, and fold it through once before mounding the rice onto a plate.
Scatter the garlic chips over the top, along with the spring onion if using.
The chips go on at the last moment, because they soften as soon as they meet the hot rice.

steps.title: Butter bread
points: Spread softened butter over one face of each slice, right out to the crust.
Those buttered faces go against the pan, so leave them facing up while you build.
Corners brown last and dry out first, so give them a little extra.

steps.title: Grate cheese
points: Grate the cheese on the coarse side, or tear slices into rough pieces.
A block grated fresh melts more evenly than pre-grated cheese, which is dusted with starch to stop it clumping.
Keep it in a loose pile rather than pressing it down.

steps.title: Build sandwich
points: Turn one slice butter side down and smear the mustard over the dry face.
Pile the cheese on evenly, grind on the pepper, then top with the second slice, butter side up.
Keep the cheese about 1 cm short of the edges, since it spreads as it melts.

steps.title: Toast first side
points: Set the pan over medium-low heat and lay the sandwich in.
Press it flat with the spatula and toast for 3 to 4 minutes, covered if you have a lid.
Lift a corner to check: deep golden is right, and the cheese at the edges should be starting to soften.

steps.title: Flip and finish
points: Slide the spatula fully under the sandwich and flip it in one move.
Press again and toast for another 3 minutes.
It is done when cheese bubbles out of the sides and the sandwich feels solid rather than loose under the spatula.

steps.title: Rest and cut
points: Move it to a board and wait one minute before cutting.
Cut it in half on the diagonal and eat it straight away.
That minute lets the cheese set just enough to stay in the sandwich instead of running onto the board.

steps.title: Cut chicken
points: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces, about 2 cm.
Season the pieces with the salt.
Wash the board and knife before anything else touches them.

steps.title: Dice onion
points: Dice the onion into small pieces, around 5 mm.
That is the last of the knife work.

steps.title: Brown chicken
points: Heat the oil over medium-high.
Lay the chicken in skin side down and leave it for 2 to 3 minutes, until well browned.
Flip and cook 1 minute more. It can stay slightly underdone, it finishes with the rice.

steps.title: Soften onion
points: Add the onion to the pan.
Cook for about 2 minutes, stirring, until translucent.

steps.title: Heat rice
points: Microwave the packed rice as directed.
Keep it hot and within reach for the last two steps.

steps.title: Fry ketchup
points: Push everything to one side and squeeze the ketchup onto the empty half.
Let it bubble for 30 seconds, stirring just the ketchup.
It is ready when it darkens slightly and smells sweet instead of sharp.

steps.title: Add rice
points: Add the hot rice and break it up with the spatula.
Fold until every grain is evenly orange, about 2 minutes.
Add the butter or soy sauce now if using, then finish with black pepper.

steps.title: Plate chicken rice
points: Taste, and adjust with a pinch of salt if needed.
Mound it onto a plate.
A little extra ketchup on top is traditional, and a fried egg is even better.

title: Kimchi Fried Rice
ingredients: 50 g (1/3 bag) or 2 rashers frozen seafood mix or bacon
Salt and black pepper (a pinch of each)
optional: Chopped scallion or toasted sesame (a little)

steps.title: Snip kimchi
points: Put the kimchi in a small bowl with its juice.
Snip it into bite-size pieces with kitchen scissors.
Keep about a tablespoon of the juice in the bowl: it is seasoning.

steps.title: Dice onion
points: Cut the onion into pieces about 5 mm across.
Match the size of the shrimp in the seafood mix.

steps.title: Heat rice
points: Microwave the pack for 2 minutes.
Open it and let the steam escape while you cook.
Slightly dry rice fries better than fresh, moist rice.

steps.title: Cook seafood
points: Seafood: melt 1 tbsp of butter over medium-high, add the mix from frozen, and cook 3 minutes until the shrimp turn opaque.
Bacon: skip the butter, snip it into 1 cm strips, and fry 3 minutes until the edges crisp.
Move it to a plate and leave everything it rendered in the pan.

steps.title: Boil off liquid
points: After seafood, let the liquid bubble away for about a minute, until the pan is nearly dry.
After bacon, the rendered fat is ready as it is.

steps.title: Fry onion and kimchi
points: Add the remaining 1/2 tbsp of butter, holding some back if the bacon left plenty of fat.
Fry the onion, and the garlic if using, for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add the kimchi, its juice, and the sugar, and fry 2 minutes more.

steps.title: Add rice
points: For the egg, push everything to one side, crack it into the bare half, and scramble it loosely for 20 seconds.
Add the rice, break up the lumps, and mix until every grain is evenly colored.
Press it flat and leave it a minute so the bottom toasts, then turn it over and press again.

steps.title: Add soy sauce
points: Pour the soy sauce onto the bare metal around the edge so it scorches for a second, then stir it through.
Return the seafood or bacon and season with salt and pepper.
Toss for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Plate fried rice
points: Kill the heat and stir in the sesame oil if you have it.
Scatter over the scallion or sesame.
Serve straight away.

steps.title: Mix sauce
points: Combine the soy sauce, sugar, sake, and water in a small bowl.
Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the ginger now if you are using it.

steps.title: Slice onion
points: Peel the onion and halve it lengthwise.
Slice with the grain into pieces about 5 mm thick.
Wash the board and knife now: the pork needs no cutting.

steps.title: Brown pork
points: Heat the oil over medium-high, or skip the oil if the pork is fatty.
Spread the pork so the pieces overlap as little as possible, then leave it alone for 1 to 2 minutes.
Flip only once the underside is well browned.

steps.title: Soften onion
points: Push the meat to one side and add the onion to the empty half.
Cook for about 2 minutes, until translucent with lightly colored edges.

steps.title: Reduce sauce
points: Pour in the sauce and keep it at a lively bubble, shaking the pan, for 1 to 2 minutes.
Kill the heat once it thickens, clings to the meat, and turns glossy.
Add the butter off the heat and let the residual warmth melt it.

steps.title: Heat rice
points: Heat the packed rice as directed.
Tip it into a deep bowl.

steps.title: Assemble bowl
points: Pile the pork and onion over the rice.
Scrape every last bit of sauce from the pan over the top.

steps.title: Cut bacon
points: Cut the bacon into strips about 1 cm wide.
This is the only knife work in the recipe.

steps.title: Fry bacon
points: Put the strips in a dry frying pan.
Cook over medium heat for about a minute.
The fat that renders out becomes your cooking oil.

steps.title: Add rice
points: Tip in the rice as it comes, unwashed.
Stir for a minute, until every grain is coated in fat.
Stop when the rice turns faintly translucent.

steps.title: Add water and bouillon
points: Pour in 400 ml of water and drop in the bouillon cube.
Break the cube up with the spatula as you stir.
Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil.

steps.title: Simmer rice
points: Drop to low heat once it boils.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Stir slowly from the bottom about every 3 minutes.

steps.title: Check rice
points: Crush a grain of rice and taste it.
Still chalky in the center: add 50 ml of water and simmer 3 minutes more.
Soupy: raise to medium heat for about a minute to drive off the excess.

steps.title: Add cheese and butter
points: Kill the heat first.
Add the 2 tablespoons of grated cheese and 10 g of butter, and stir for about 20 seconds.
Season with salt and black pepper.

title: Seafood Curry
ingredients: 1 pack per person microwavable packed rice

steps.title: Cut carrots
points: Cut the carrots into thin quarter-rounds, about 3 mm thick.
Two small carrots are about a handful of slices.

steps.title: Slice onion
points: Slice the onion thinly.
Keep it about as fine as the carrots so both cook in the same time.

steps.title: Fry vegetables
points: Melt 1 tbsp of butter over medium heat.
Add the carrots and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the onion and cook 3 minutes more, until translucent.

steps.title: Simmer vegetables
points: Add 250 ml of water and bring it to a boil.
Drop the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes.

steps.title: Add roux
points: Turn the heat off first.
Break in the 2 blocks and stir until completely dissolved.

steps.title: Add seafood
points: Add the seafood straight from frozen.
Return to low heat and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring gently.

steps.title: Heat rice
points: Microwave the rice for 2 minutes.
Turn it out onto a plate and fluff it with a spoon.

steps.title: Serve curry
points: Stir the last of the butter through the pan off the heat.
Ladle the curry beside the rice rather than on top.
Eat while it's hot.

steps.title: Mix egg and cheese
points: Beat both eggs and the parmesan together in a small bowl.
Add a generous grind of pepper.
Set the bowl next to the stove.

steps.title: Cut bacon
points: Cut the bacon into batons about 1 cm thick.
This is the only knife work in the recipe.

steps.title: Brown bacon
points: Put the bacon in the cold pan, then turn the heat to medium.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the fat runs and the edges crisp.
Add the olive oil only if the bacon is very lean.

steps.title: Boil water
points: Leave the bacon and all its fat in the pan.
Pour in the water and the salt.
Bring it to a boil.

steps.title: Add spaghetti
points: Lay the spaghetti in whole, fanned across the pan, and let the submerged ends soften for about 30 seconds.
Press the standing ends down with the tongs until every strand is under.
Cook uncovered for the time on the packet, usually 8 to 9 minutes.

steps.title: Reduce liquid
points: Keep it at a steady bubble, stirring now and then.
Aim for about two spoonfuls of starchy, cloudy liquid left when the pasta is done.
Add a splash of water if it dries out early, or boil it off if there's too much.

steps.title: Add egg mixture
points: Turn the heat off and let the pan stop bubbling, about 45 seconds.
Pour in the egg mixture and toss fast with the tongs.
The residual heat and starchy liquid turn it into a glossy cream.

steps.title: Plate carbonara
points: Twirl it onto a plate.
Scrape the sauce left in the pan over the top.
Finish with more black pepper and a little extra parmesan if you like.

steps.title: Cut tomatoes
points: Cut each tomato into 6 to 8 wedges.
Keep the juice and seeds, they become the sauce.
Cut the spring onion into short pieces and keep the green tops separate.

steps.title: Beat eggs
points: Crack the eggs into a bowl with a pinch of salt and the white pepper.
Beat until the yolks and whites are one color, about 20 seconds.
Stop there. Beating longer makes them thin and rubbery.

steps.title: Heat pan
points: Put 1 tbsp of the oil in over medium-high and wait until it thins out and shimmers.
A drop of egg should sizzle and puff immediately.
A cold pan is the main reason eggs stick.

steps.title: Scramble eggs
points: Pour the eggs in and leave them for 10 seconds, until the edges set.
Push the set parts to the middle with the spatula in slow, large sweeps.
Take them out while the middle still looks wet, about 30 seconds in total.

steps.title: Cook tomatoes
points: Add the remaining oil and the white parts of the spring onion, then the tomato wedges.
Press them gently with the spatula and cook 3 to 4 minutes.
They are ready when the skins slip loose and there is a pool of red juice in the pan.

steps.title: Season sauce
points: Stir in the sugar, a good pinch of salt, and the ketchup if you are using it.
Taste the juice now. It should be sweet first and sour second.
Let it bubble for another minute so it thickens slightly.

steps.title: Return eggs
points: Slide the eggs back in and fold them through the sauce two or three times.
Kill the heat after 30 seconds, while the curds are still in large pieces.
Finish with the green spring onion tops and a few drops of sesame oil, and serve it over rice.

steps.title: Cut hard vegetables
points: Cut the carrot into thin strips and the onion into wedges about 1 cm thick.
These two go in first and take the longest, so keep them thinner than everything else.
Put them together in one pile.

steps.title: Cut soft vegetables
points: Cut the cabbage into rough 4 cm squares and the bell pepper into strips.
Slice the mushrooms about 5 mm thick.
Keep this second pile separate from the first.

steps.title: Prep aromatics
points: Chop the garlic and the ginger finely.
Cut the spring onion into short pieces, keeping the white and green parts apart.
Rinse the bean sprouts and shake them as dry as you can.

steps.title: Mix sauce
points: Stir the soy sauce and bouillon powder together in a small bowl.
Dissolving the powder now stops it clumping in the pan.
Set the bowl next to the stove, the pan work runs without pauses.

steps.title: Fry aromatics
points: Heat the oil over medium, then add the garlic, ginger, and the white spring onion.
Stir for about 30 seconds, until you can smell them.
Keep the heat off high here, garlic burns bitter in seconds.

steps.title: Add hard vegetables
points: Turn the heat to high and add the carrot and onion.
Stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the onion edges turn clear.
The carrot should still be firm, it keeps cooking to the end.

steps.title: Add soft vegetables
points: Add the cabbage, bell pepper, and mushrooms all at once.
Let the pile sit for 1 minute without touching it, then toss.
Repeat twice: rest, toss, rest. About 3 minutes in total.

steps.title: Add bean sprouts
points: Tip in the bean sprouts and toss for 1 minute, no longer.
They should still squeak against your teeth.
Anything more and they go limp and start weeping water.

steps.title: Add sauce
points: Pour the soy and bouillon mixture around the edge of the pan.
Toss everything for 30 seconds, then kill the heat.
Taste before adding salt, then finish with black pepper, the green spring onion, and the sesame oil.

steps.title: Cut vegetables
points: Cut the cabbage into rough 3 cm squares, the onion into thin wedges, and the carrot into thin strips.
Keep the carrot thinner than everything else, it is the slowest to soften.
Pile it all on one corner of the board so you can tip it in at once.

steps.title: Cut pork
points: Cut the pork slices into pieces about 4 cm wide.
Long strips tangle in the noodles later and come out in one clump.

steps.title: Loosen noodles
points: Open the pack and pull the noodle brick apart with your fingers.
They come out compressed and stuck together, and separating them dry is much easier than fighting them in a hot pan.

steps.title: Brown pork
points: Heat the oil over medium-high, then spread the pork in one layer.
Cook about 2 minutes without moving it, until the edges are browned.
Season it with a little black pepper here.

steps.title: Add vegetables
points: Tip in the carrot, onion, and cabbage together.
Toss for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cabbage has wilted but still has bite.
The pork fat coats everything, so nothing should stick yet.

steps.title: Steam noodles
points: Lay the loosened noodles over the top, pour the water around them, and cover.
Leave it 1 minute, then take the lid off and toss everything together.
The noodles should be hot, glossy, and moving freely.

steps.title: Add sauce
points: Pour the yakisoba sauce around the edge of the pan, not onto the noodles.
Toss hard for about 1 minute, until every strand is the same brown.
Let it sit still for the last 20 seconds so the sauce catches on the pan and turns fragrant.

steps.title: Plate
points: Pile it onto a plate while everything is still steaming.
Add a pinch of aonori and a small heap of pickled ginger on the side if you have them.
Grind over more black pepper and eat it straight away.
